analysis.cross_scope_synthesis: Across the three scoped sources one pattern holds: the package separates measured water kLa rows (32.6 and 38.8 h-1 at a single shared airflow of 0.51 L/min), author-calculated quantities (power densities via Junker 2004, tip speeds, a unitless geometry ratio of 40.8), and declared scenario assumptions (gas exponent 0.5, power screen 1000 W/m3, 300 rpm, 0.25 vvm at a 20 L receiver). The mirrored equipment blocks in literature-excerpts.txt and model-input.json agree with each other for all three vessels on impeller type, blade counts, submerged counts, diameters and blade heights - independently confirmed by the specialist consistency sub-investigation (specialist-1), which also confirmed the micro-sparger basis contradiction and the pressure mismatch. The same missing-characterization list recurs at every scale: no certified pressure, motor, torque or speed limits, no sparger orifice geometry, no tank diameter, and no validated broth kLa response surface; the 200 L receiver additionally lacks viability and valid off-gas data. The evidence platform's deterministic metric layer found no numeric observation cells in the scoped ingestion, so no report-level metric could be arithmetically certified; every numerical result here is either a transcribed source line or an output of the versioned fermentation_transfer host tool run under declared assumptions, independently re-derived in the investigation kernel with exact agreement (power exponent 0.1884, agitation exponent 0.5084; 20 L at 300 rpm and 0.25 vvm: 460.59 W/m3 and kLa 36.22 h-1). The two ring-sparger rows anchor the fitted power law with zero residual degrees of freedom; the identical airflow makes the gas exponent unidentifiable, and the 38.8 h-1 reference target carries a micro-sparger basis label that no scoped row supports. Consequences: the declared 300 rpm/0.25 vvm scenario fails the nominal kLa target under every gas-exponent value swept (modeled kLa 36.00-36.58 h-1); the conditional lowest-power passes (275 rpm at 0.35 vvm for 20 L at 354.77 W/m3 and kLa 40.80 h-1; 150 rpm at 0.35 vvm for 200 L at 317.46 W/m3 and kLa 39.95 h-1) are not robust to the declared sensitivity; and the preferred-strategy ranking reorders completely between gas-exponent assumptions of 0 and 0.8 (20 L lowest-power pass at 350 rpm and 0.15 vvm vs 225 rpm and 0.35 vvm). Copying the source recipe costs 763.19 W/m3 at 20 L (kLa 40.23 h-1) and 4208.27 W/m3 at 200 L (kLa 55.49 h-1), the latter about 4.2x the assumed power screen with tip speed 3.72 m/s. The scenario file's gauge pressure (100 kPa vs published 0.1-0.3 bar overhead), its kLa entry (20 h-1 vs the 38.8 h-1 target) and its OUR/solubility/cost entries are either unreconciled with or unused by the sulfolobus model, although its own numbers are internally self-consistent for oxygen transfer (20 x (7.5 x 0.7 - 1.5) = 75 mg/L/h vs assumed OUR 50 mg/L/h). Nothing in scope certifies a receiver operating point; withheld receiving outcomes and evaluator-only article access remain explicit gaps, and the 200 L data-quality caveats block process-level validation there.
analysis.assessment: The scoped package frames an aerobic-fermentation scale-transfer problem: match a source bioreactor's measured oxygen-transfer coefficient at larger receivers using two water-calibration summaries, published impeller geometry, and declared scenario assumptions. The transfer problem is reconstructed; it is not certified. The two calibration rows share a single airflow, so the gas-flow exponent is unidentified and every modeled receiver kLa is assumption-driven; the fitted power law has zero residual degrees of freedom and rests on rounded published summaries. The declared operating point fails the nominal kLa matching criterion under every gas-exponent value swept, and the conditional lowest-power screen passes are not robust to the declared sensitivity. Copying the source recipe is power-inefficient at the largest receiver. Rated equipment limits, tank diameter, sparger geometry, receiver broth characterization, oxygen uptake and medium solubility are absent, so no operating strategy can be certified and no oxygen-feasibility or biological-outcome claim is available. Every numerical result is a published summary, an author-calculated value, a fitted parameter, or a scenario assumption; none is a receiver measurement. The reference target's basis label conflicts with the scoped ring-sparger rows and stays unresolved. Engineering follow-up: characterize receiver broth kLa and the gas-flow exponent, obtain certified equipment limits, and reconcile the reference basis before any recipe decision. No equipment approval or control action is proposed here. Status: submitted as a partial investigation. interpretations.statement: The scoped package separates three evidence classes - direct water measurements (the two kLa rows), author-calculated or fitted quantities (power densities, tip speeds, geometry ratio), and declared scenario assumptions - and the transfer analysis inherits the weakest class: with both calibration rows at one airflow, gas-flow dependence is unidentified and any single recommended operating point is assumption-driven rather than measured.

Under the versioned transfer model the declared operating point does not meet the nominal kLa matching criterion for any gas-exponent value in the swept range, so its screen failure is robust to the unidentified exponent even though every other strategy ranking is not.

Copying the source recipe (same rpm and same specific airflow) is not power-neutral: receiver geometry with more submerged impellers and larger impeller diameters changes power density sharply, and at the largest receiver the modeled power density exceeds the assumed power screen by roughly a factor of four - a modeled result conditional on the constant turbulent power-number and gassing-factor hypotheses, not a measurement.

No absolute oxygen-feasibility claim is available: OUR, process-medium oxygen solubility and absolute DO for the Sulfolobus process are absent from the scoped evidence, and the scenario file's oxygen-uptake, solubility, saturation and price entries are declared assumptions that the versioned sulfolobus transfer model does not consume.

The reference target's basis label conflicts with the scoped calibration rows: the target value is labeled micro-sparger-based, but the only rows carrying that value in the fully-read package are ring-sparger rows, and no micro-sparger row exists in scope; either the label is inaccurate or the underlying row was withheld with the evaluator-only article, and the conflict cannot be resolved within scope.

The scenario's declared gauge pressure sits well above the published receiver overhead pressure range and is not reconciled with it, although the sulfolobus transfer model does not consume the pressure assumption. The overhead (gauge) reading of the published range is the consistent interpretation: an absolute reading would place the published range below one atmosphere and contradict the slight-overhead wording. This is a reconciliation gap between the scenario file and the cultivation evidence, not an equipment claim.

Process-level validation of any transfer strategy at the largest receiver is blocked by the reported data quality: viability was not measured and off-gas data were faulty there, and the calibration medium was water rather than fermentation broth, so modeled kLa matches cannot be read as biological success.

draft_report.assessment: The scoped package frames an aerobic-fermentation scale-transfer problem: match a source bioreactor's measured oxygen-transfer coefficient at larger receivers using two water-calibration summaries, published impeller geometry, and declared scenario assumptions. The transfer problem is reconstructed; it is not certified. The two calibration rows share a single airflow, so the gas-flow exponent is unidentified and every modeled receiver kLa is assumption-driven; the fitted power law has zero residual degrees of freedom and rests on rounded published summaries. The declared operating point fails the nominal kLa matching criterion under every gas-exponent value swept, and the conditional lowest-power screen passes are not robust to the declared sensitivity. Copying the source recipe is power-inefficient at the largest receiver. Rated equipment limits, tank diameter, sparger geometry, receiver broth characterization, oxygen uptake and medium solubility are absent, so no operating strategy can be certified and no oxygen-feasibility or biological-outcome claim is available. Every numerical result is a published summary, an author-calculated value, a fitted parameter, or a scenario assumption; none is a receiver measurement. The reference target's basis label conflicts with the scoped ring-sparger rows and stays unresolved. Engineering follow-up: characterize receiver broth kLa and the gas-flow exponent, obtain certified equipment limits, and reconcile the reference basis before any recipe decision. No equipment approval or control action is proposed here. Status: submitted as a partial investigation. The classified claim ledger covers the interpretation and hypothesis statements; the numeric observed-fact statements cannot be linked to numeric evidence rows because the scoped ingestion contains text-only lines with no numeric cells, so independent human review of those numeric statements against the original sources remains required.

observed_facts.statement: The scoped literature package is a reviewed, calibration-only excerpt set from Rastaedter 2023 (DOI 10.3389/fbioe.2023.1160012); the full article and supplement are evaluator/research-only during the blinded benchmark and contain the receiving outcomes.

The model input is classified as a reviewed published summary, not an autonomous extraction, and its citation locations are Main section 2.1 with Table 2 (source 2 L only) and Supplement Table S1 (impeller geometry).

Calibration row source_ring_355 (Table 2, 2 L ring sparger at 355 rpm) reports working volume 2 L, ring sparger, 355 rpm, airflow 0.51 L/min, kLa 32.6 h-1, aerated power density 0.25 kW/m3, impeller tip speed 0.97 m/s, and a reported geometry ratio of 40.8.

Calibration row source_ring_500 (Table 2, 2 L ring sparger at 500 rpm) reports the same 2 L working volume, ring sparger and 0.51 L/min airflow, with 500 rpm, kLa 38.8 h-1, aerated power density 0.63 kW/m3, impeller tip speed 1.36 m/s, and the same reported geometry ratio 40.8.

The kLa characterization was performed in deionized water at 75 degrees C using an N2-to-air dynamic DO transition with DO calibrated at each airflow; the author-reported kla standard deviation is 1.17 h-1 and is explicitly an average measurement spread across kLa determinations, not a row-specific confidence interval and not prediction uncertainty.
The model input itself states the limitation that the two ring-source points have identical airflow, so the gas exponent is unidentifiable.

Per-field classifications in the excerpts mark kLa as experimental water characterization, aerated power density as author-calculated using Junker 2004, impeller tip speed as author-calculated, the geometry ratio as an author-reported ratio whose unit is not stated in the header, and rpm as a published operating setting that is not a hardware limit.

The source bioreactor is a Sartorius Biostat A-plus with 2 L working / 3 L total volume, a Rushton impeller type, six blades per impeller, two submerged impellers, 52 mm impeller diameter and 10 mm impeller blade height.

The selected receiver is an Infors HT Techfors S with 20 L working / 30 L total volume, Rushton impellers, six blades per impeller, three submerged impellers, 95 mm impeller diameter and 13.22 mm impeller blade height.

The largest receiver is a Heinrich Frings Proreact 20P with 200 L working / 300 L total volume, Rushton impellers, six blades per impeller, four submerged impellers, 200 mm impeller diameter and 40 mm impeller blade height.

Every equipment entry lists the same missing fields: vessel rated maximum pressure, motor power rating, maximum safe rpm, maximum safe torque, sparger orifice geometry, and a validated broth kLa response surface.

Tank diameter is null for all three vessels; the excerpts state that no direct tank diameter appears in the main Table 2 or Supplement S1, that the reported geometry ratio of 40.8 has no unit in the header, and that a measured diameter must not be silently reconstructed.

The model input declares a reference kLa of 38.8 h-1 as the target matching criterion with the basis 'Source 2 L micro-sparger, Table 2', explicitly not a receiver validation; within the fully-read scoped package the only calibration rows carrying 38.8 h-1 are ring-sparger rows, and no micro-sparger calibration row exists in the scoped excerpts.

Cultivation conditions are Sulfolobus acidocaldarius DSM 639 at 75 degrees C and pH 3.0 with an imposed dilution rate of 0.03 h-1; slight overhead pressure of 0.1 to 0.3 bar was applied during the 20 L and 200 L cultivations with the exact value per receiver not reported; the nominal fed-batch growth rate is 0.035 h-1 while the measured specific growth rate is null, with a note that physiology plots show comparable growth rates but no numerical summary and that a measured estimate must not be equated with the imposed dilution rate; batch carbon sources are monosodium glutamate 2 g/L, d-glucose 1 g/L and NZ-amine 0.25 g/L.

The model input's own limitations state that water characterization at 75 degrees C is not fermentation-broth validation, that 200 L viability was not measured and 200 L off-gas data were faulty, and that rated equipment limits are unavailable so scenario bounds are assumptions, never certified limits.

The declared missing inputs for the transfer are the receiver broth kLa response surface, the gas-flow exponent at the source scale, sparger geometry and gassed power corrections, OUR and process-medium oxygen solubility, and certified pressure, motor, torque and speed limits.

The scenario file declares assumption values including gas exponent 0.5, power screen 1000 W/m3, selected receiver 20 L, rpm 300, airflow 0.25 vvm, gauge pressure 100 kPa, ambient 101.325 kPa, air 36 Nm3/h, oxygen 2 Nm3/h, compressor efficiency 0.65, inlet temperature 303.15 K, electricity 0.12 USD/kWh, oxygen 0.2 USD/Nm3, comparison horizon 120 h, air saturation 7.5 mg/L, broth solubility factor 0.7, kLa 20 h-1, dissolved oxygen 1.5 mg/L, OUR 50 mg/L/h, no extra methanol, and methanol 0.5 USD/L; these are scenario bounds, not certified limits or measurements.

The mirrored equipment blocks in literature-excerpts.txt and model-input.json agree with each other for all three vessels on impeller type, blade count, submerged impeller count, impeller diameter and blade height (2 L: Rushton, six blades, two submerged, 52 mm, 10 mm; 20 L: three submerged, 95 mm, 13.22 mm; 200 L: four submerged, 200 mm, 40 mm), and on the same missing rated-limit, sparger-orifice and broth-kLa fields; an independent specialist sub-investigation reached the same cross-file agreement.

interpretations.statement: The scoped package separates three evidence classes - direct water measurements (the two kLa rows), author-calculated or fitted quantities (power densities, tip speeds, geometry ratio), and declared scenario assumptions - and the transfer analysis inherits the weakest class: with both calibration rows at one airflow, gas-flow dependence is unidentified and any single recommended operating point is assumption-driven rather than measured.

Under the versioned transfer model the declared operating point does not meet the nominal kLa matching criterion for any gas-exponent value in the swept range, so its screen failure is robust to the unidentified exponent even though every other strategy ranking is not.

Copying the source recipe (same rpm and same specific airflow) is not power-neutral: receiver geometry with more submerged impellers and larger impeller diameters changes power density sharply, and at the largest receiver the modeled power density exceeds the assumed power screen by roughly a factor of four - a modeled result conditional on the constant turbulent power-number and gassing-factor hypotheses, not a measurement.

No absolute oxygen-feasibility claim is available: OUR, process-medium oxygen solubility and absolute DO for the Sulfolobus process are absent from the scoped evidence, and the scenario file's oxygen-uptake, solubility, saturation and price entries are declared assumptions that the versioned sulfolobus transfer model does not consume.

The reference target's basis label conflicts with the scoped calibration rows: the target value is labeled micro-sparger-based, but the only rows carrying that value in the fully-read package are ring-sparger rows, and no micro-sparger row exists in scope; either the label is inaccurate or the underlying row was withheld with the evaluator-only article, and the conflict cannot be resolved within scope.

The scenario's declared gauge pressure sits well above the published receiver overhead pressure range and is not reconciled with it, although the sulfolobus transfer model does not consume the pressure assumption. The overhead (gauge) reading of the published range is the consistent interpretation: an absolute reading would place the published range below one atmosphere and contradict the slight-overhead wording. This is a reconciliation gap between the scenario file and the cultivation evidence, not an equipment claim.

Process-level validation of any transfer strategy at the largest receiver is blocked by the reported data quality: viability was not measured and off-gas data were faulty there, and the calibration medium was water rather than fermentation broth, so modeled kLa matches cannot be read as biological success.

resolved_questions.question: What does the versioned transfer model compute from the scoped calibration and the declared scenario?
resolved_questions.finding: Modeled values from the host fermentation_transfer tool (registered deterministic characterization; scenario assumptions are not measurements), independently re-derived in the investigation kernel with exact agreement: fitted power exponent 0.1884 and agitation exponent 0.5084 from the two rounded ring-sparger summaries (residual degrees of freedom 0, gas exponent unidentified, anchored at source kLa 32.6 h-1 and source power 250 W/m3). For the declared scenario (20 L receiver, 300 rpm, 0.25 vvm = 5.0 L/min) the model gives power density 460.59 W/m3, hydrodynamic power 9.21 W, tip speed 1.49 m/s, predicted kLa 36.22 h-1 with declared sensitivity 18.00-73.15 h-1 (assumed gas exponent 0-0.8 and receiver geometry multiplier 0.5-2, explicitly not calibrated confidence bounds). The scenario grid marks this point screen_reject because predicted kLa is below the 38.8 h-1 nominal target.

resolved_questions.question: Which conditional operating strategies does the screen accept, and how do they compare?
resolved_questions.finding: Modeled results under the assumed gas exponent 0.5 and power screen 1000 W/m3: the 84-point grid yields 7 conditional passes at the 20 L receiver and 7 at the 200 L receiver; none is robust to the declared sensitivity (every sensitivity low bound is below the 38.8 h-1 target). Lowest-power conditional passes: 275 rpm at 0.35 vvm (354.77 W/m3, predicted kLa 40.80 h-1, hydrodynamic power 7.10 W, tip speed 1.37 m/s) at 20 L, and 150 rpm at 0.35 vvm (317.46 W/m3, kLa 39.95 h-1, 63.49 W, 1.57 m/s) at 200 L; both carry status conditional_screen_pass_requires_characterization, approval_status engineering_review_required, rated_equipment_feasibility unknown. Copy-source-recipe points (355 rpm, 0.255 vvm): 763.19 W/m3 with kLa 40.23 h-1 at 20 L (inside the assumed screen) and 4208.27 W/m3 with kLa 55.49 h-1 and tip speed 3.72 m/s at 200 L (about 4.2x the assumed power screen).

resolved_questions.question: How does the unidentified gas exponent change the conditional strategy comparison?
resolved_questions.finding: Modeled re-runs of the same tool with only the gas exponent changed: at gas exponent 0 the lowest-power conditional pass moves to 350 rpm at 0.15 vvm (731.4 W/m3, kLa 39.9 h-1) at 20 L and 195 rpm at 0.15 vvm (697.5 W/m3, kLa 39.6 h-1) at 200 L; at gas exponent 0.8 it moves to 225 rpm at 0.35 vvm (194.3 W/m3, kLa 40.1 h-1) at 20 L and 135 rpm at 0.35 vvm (231.4 W/m3, kLa 41.4 h-1) at 200 L. Across the same sweep the declared point's predicted kLa spans only 36.00-36.58 h-1, remaining below the 38.8 h-1 target, so the declared point's failure is robust to the gas-exponent assumption while every preferred-strategy ranking is not.

resolved_questions.question: Can absolute oxygen feasibility (oxygen transfer vs uptake) be assessed for the receiver?
resolved_questions.finding: No. The versioned tool returns no oxygen-capacity result for this case and states that Cstar, absolute DO and OUR are not tabulated, so no absolute culture oxygen-feasibility claim is possible. The scenario file's OUR (50 mg/L/h), dissolved oxygen (1.5 mg/L), broth solubility factor (0.7), air saturation (7.5 mg/L), gas-flow, compressor and price entries are declared scenario assumptions that the sulfolobus transfer model does not consume; treating them as Sulfolobus process measurements would be unsupported.

resolved_questions.question: What receiver characterization is missing before any transfer decision?
resolved_questions.finding: The scoped package's own missing-input list: receiver broth kLa response surface, gas-flow exponent at the source scale, sparger geometry and gassed power corrections, OUR and process-medium oxygen solubility, and certified pressure, motor, torque and speed limits. Every equipment entry additionally lists vessel rated max pressure, motor power rating, maximum safe rpm, maximum safe torque, sparger orifice geometry and validated broth kLa response surface as missing; tank diameter is null for all three vessels with an explicit instruction not to reconstruct it from the unitless reported ratio.

resolved_questions.question: Do the scenario assumptions reconcile with the published receiver conditions?
resolved_questions.finding: Partially. The declared gauge pressure of 100 kPa is roughly three to ten times the published receiver overhead pressure range of 0.1-0.3 bar (exact value per receiver not reported), and it is not consumed by the sulfolobus transfer model; the declared rpm 300 and 0.25 vvm at the 20 L receiver are plausible published-operating-setting-style values but the model input marks rpm values as operating settings rather than hardware limits, and no receiver-side operating record exists in scope to confirm them.

resolved_questions.question: Do the scenario file's mass-transfer assumptions reconcile internally and with the declared kLa target?
resolved_questions.finding: Partially, and with one open conflict. The scenario file declares kLa 20 h-1, air saturation 7.5 mg/L, broth solubility factor 0.7, dissolved oxygen 1.5 mg/L and OUR 50 mg/L/h - all assumptions, none a measurement, and none consumed by the sulfolobus transfer model. Internal arithmetic on these declared values gives 20 x (7.5 x 0.7 - 1.5) = 75 mg/L/h, above the assumed OUR of 50 mg/L/h, so the assumed DO setpoint is attainable under the scenario's own numbers; this is arithmetic on assumptions, not evidence of real receiver performance. The scenario's kLa entry of 20 h-1 is about half the declared 38.8 h-1 reference target, so whether it is a deliberate de-rated receiver target or an inconsistency with the matching criterion stays open, and no saturation value in the file carries a stated temperature basis while cultivation runs at 75 degrees C.

draft_report.cross_scope_synthesis: Across the three scoped sources one pattern holds: the package separates measured water kLa rows (32.6 and 38.8 h-1 at a single shared airflow of 0.51 L/min), author-calculated quantities (power densities via Junker 2004, tip speeds, a unitless geometry ratio of 40.8), and declared scenario assumptions (gas exponent 0.5, power screen 1000 W/m3, 300 rpm, 0.25 vvm at a 20 L receiver). The mirrored equipment blocks in literature-excerpts.txt and model-input.json agree with each other for all three vessels on impeller type, blade counts, submerged counts, diameters and blade heights - independently confirmed by the specialist consistency sub-investigation (specialist-1), which also confirmed the micro-sparger basis contradiction and the pressure mismatch. The same missing-characterization list recurs at every scale: no certified pressure, motor, torque or speed limits, no sparger orifice geometry, no tank diameter, and no validated broth kLa response surface; the 200 L receiver additionally lacks viability and valid off-gas data. The evidence platform's deterministic metric layer found no numeric observation cells in the scoped ingestion, so no report-level metric could be arithmetically certified; every numerical result here is either a transcribed source line or an output of the versioned fermentation_transfer host tool run under declared assumptions, independently re-derived in the investigation kernel with exact agreement (power exponent 0.1884, agitation exponent 0.5084; 20 L at 300 rpm and 0.25 vvm: 460.59 W/m3 and kLa 36.22 h-1). The two ring-sparger rows anchor the fitted power law with zero residual degrees of freedom; the identical airflow makes the gas exponent unidentifiable, and the 38.8 h-1 reference target carries a micro-sparger basis label that no scoped row supports. Consequences: the declared 300 rpm/0.25 vvm scenario fails the nominal kLa target under every gas-exponent value swept (modeled kLa 36.00-36.58 h-1); the conditional lowest-power passes (275 rpm at 0.35 vvm for 20 L at 354.77 W/m3 and kLa 40.80 h-1; 150 rpm at 0.35 vvm for 200 L at 317.46 W/m3 and kLa 39.95 h-1) are not robust to the declared sensitivity; and the preferred-strategy ranking reorders completely between gas-exponent assumptions of 0 and 0.8 (20 L lowest-power pass at 350 rpm and 0.15 vvm vs 225 rpm and 0.35 vvm). Copying the source recipe costs 763.19 W/m3 at 20 L (kLa 40.23 h-1) and 4208.27 W/m3 at 200 L (kLa 55.49 h-1), the latter about 4.2x the assumed power screen with tip speed 3.72 m/s. The scenario file's gauge pressure (100 kPa vs published 0.1-0.3 bar overhead), its kLa entry (20 h-1 vs the 38.8 h-1 target) and its OUR/solubility/cost entries are either unreconciled with or unused by the sulfolobus model, although its own numbers are internally self-consistent for oxygen transfer (20 x (7.5 x 0.7 - 1.5) = 75 mg/L/h vs assumed OUR 50 mg/L/h). Nothing in scope certifies a receiver operating point; withheld receiving outcomes and evaluator-only article access remain explicit gaps, and the 200 L data-quality caveats block process-level validation there.

resolved_questions.question: What does the versioned transfer model compute from the scoped calibration and the declared scenario?
resolved_questions.finding: Modeled values from the host fermentation_transfer tool (registered deterministic characterization; scenario assumptions are not measurements), independently re-derived in the investigation kernel with exact agreement: fitted power exponent 0.1884 and agitation exponent 0.5084 from the two rounded ring-sparger summaries (residual degrees of freedom 0, gas exponent unidentified, anchored at source kLa 32.6 h-1 and source power 250 W/m3). For the declared scenario (20 L receiver, 300 rpm, 0.25 vvm = 5.0 L/min) the model gives power density 460.59 W/m3, hydrodynamic power 9.21 W, tip speed 1.49 m/s, predicted kLa 36.22 h-1 with declared sensitivity 18.00-73.15 h-1 (assumed gas exponent 0-0.8 and receiver geometry multiplier 0.5-2, explicitly not calibrated confidence bounds). The scenario grid marks this point screen_reject because predicted kLa is below the 38.8 h-1 nominal target.

resolved_questions.question: Which conditional operating strategies does the screen accept, and how do they compare?
resolved_questions.finding: Modeled results under the assumed gas exponent 0.5 and power screen 1000 W/m3: the 84-point grid yields 7 conditional passes at the 20 L receiver and 7 at the 200 L receiver; none is robust to the declared sensitivity (every sensitivity low bound is below the 38.8 h-1 target). Lowest-power conditional passes: 275 rpm at 0.35 vvm (354.77 W/m3, predicted kLa 40.80 h-1, hydrodynamic power 7.10 W, tip speed 1.37 m/s) at 20 L, and 150 rpm at 0.35 vvm (317.46 W/m3, kLa 39.95 h-1, 63.49 W, 1.57 m/s) at 200 L; both carry status conditional_screen_pass_requires_characterization, approval_status engineering_review_required, rated_equipment_feasibility unknown. Copy-source-recipe points (355 rpm, 0.255 vvm): 763.19 W/m3 with kLa 40.23 h-1 at 20 L (inside the assumed screen) and 4208.27 W/m3 with kLa 55.49 h-1 and tip speed 3.72 m/s at 200 L (about 4.2x the assumed power screen).

resolved_questions.question: How does the unidentified gas exponent change the conditional strategy comparison?
resolved_questions.finding: Modeled re-runs of the same tool with only the gas exponent changed: at gas exponent 0 the lowest-power conditional pass moves to 350 rpm at 0.15 vvm (731.4 W/m3, kLa 39.9 h-1) at 20 L and 195 rpm at 0.15 vvm (697.5 W/m3, kLa 39.6 h-1) at 200 L; at gas exponent 0.8 it moves to 225 rpm at 0.35 vvm (194.3 W/m3, kLa 40.1 h-1) at 20 L and 135 rpm at 0.35 vvm (231.4 W/m3, kLa 41.4 h-1) at 200 L. Across the same sweep the declared point's predicted kLa spans only 36.00-36.58 h-1, remaining below the 38.8 h-1 target, so the declared point's failure is robust to the gas-exponent assumption while every preferred-strategy ranking is not.

resolved_questions.question: Can absolute oxygen feasibility (oxygen transfer vs uptake) be assessed for the receiver?
resolved_questions.finding: No. The versioned tool returns no oxygen-capacity result for this case and states that Cstar, absolute DO and OUR are not tabulated, so no absolute culture oxygen-feasibility claim is possible. The scenario file's OUR (50 mg/L/h), dissolved oxygen (1.5 mg/L), broth solubility factor (0.7), air saturation (7.5 mg/L), gas-flow, compressor and price entries are declared scenario assumptions that the sulfolobus transfer model does not consume; treating them as Sulfolobus process measurements would be unsupported.

resolved_questions.question: What receiver characterization is missing before any transfer decision?
resolved_questions.finding: The scoped package's own missing-input list: receiver broth kLa response surface, gas-flow exponent at the source scale, sparger geometry and gassed power corrections, OUR and process-medium oxygen solubility, and certified pressure, motor, torque and speed limits. Every equipment entry additionally lists vessel rated max pressure, motor power rating, maximum safe rpm, maximum safe torque, sparger orifice geometry and validated broth kLa response surface as missing; tank diameter is null for all three vessels with an explicit instruction not to reconstruct it from the unitless reported ratio.

resolved_questions.question: Do the scenario assumptions reconcile with the published receiver conditions?
resolved_questions.finding: Partially. The declared gauge pressure of 100 kPa is roughly three to ten times the published receiver overhead pressure range of 0.1-0.3 bar (exact value per receiver not reported), and it is not consumed by the sulfolobus transfer model; the declared rpm 300 and 0.25 vvm at the 20 L receiver are plausible published-operating-setting-style values but the model input marks rpm values as operating settings rather than hardware limits, and no receiver-side operating record exists in scope to confirm them.

resolved_questions.question: Do the scenario file's mass-transfer assumptions reconcile internally and with the declared kLa target?
resolved_questions.finding: Partially, and with one open conflict. The scenario file declares kLa 20 h-1, air saturation 7.5 mg/L, broth solubility factor 0.7, dissolved oxygen 1.5 mg/L and OUR 50 mg/L/h - all assumptions, none a measurement, and none consumed by the sulfolobus transfer model. Internal arithmetic on these declared values gives 20 x (7.5 x 0.7 - 1.5) = 75 mg/L/h, above the assumed OUR of 50 mg/L/h, so the assumed DO setpoint is attainable under the scenario's own numbers; this is arithmetic on assumptions, not evidence of real receiver performance. The scenario's kLa entry of 20 h-1 is about half the declared 38.8 h-1 reference target, so whether it is a deliberate de-rated receiver target or an inconsistency with the matching criterion stays open, and no saturation value in the file carries a stated temperature basis while cultivation runs at 75 degrees C.

workflow.cross_scope_synthesis: Across the three scoped sources one pattern holds: the package separates measured water kLa rows (32.6 and 38.8 h-1 at a single shared airflow of 0.51 L/min), author-calculated quantities (power densities via Junker 2004, tip speeds, a unitless geometry ratio of 40.8), and declared scenario assumptions (gas exponent 0.5, power screen 1000 W/m3, 300 rpm, 0.25 vvm at a 20 L receiver). The mirrored equipment blocks in literature-excerpts.txt and model-input.json agree with each other for all three vessels on impeller type, blade counts, submerged counts, diameters and blade heights - independently confirmed by the specialist consistency sub-investigation (specialist-1), which also confirmed the micro-sparger basis contradiction and the pressure mismatch. The same missing-characterization list recurs at every scale: no certified pressure, motor, torque or speed limits, no sparger orifice geometry, no tank diameter, and no validated broth kLa response surface; the 200 L receiver additionally lacks viability and valid off-gas data. The evidence platform's deterministic metric layer found no numeric observation cells in the scoped ingestion, so no report-level metric could be arithmetically certified; every numerical result here is either a transcribed source line or an output of the versioned fermentation_transfer host tool run under declared assumptions, independently re-derived in the investigation kernel with exact agreement (power exponent 0.1884, agitation exponent 0.5084; 20 L at 300 rpm and 0.25 vvm: 460.59 W/m3 and kLa 36.22 h-1). The two ring-sparger rows anchor the fitted power law with zero residual degrees of freedom; the identical airflow makes the gas exponent unidentifiable, and the 38.8 h-1 reference target carries a micro-sparger basis label that no scoped row supports. Consequences: the declared 300 rpm/0.25 vvm scenario fails the nominal kLa target under every gas-exponent value swept (modeled kLa 36.00-36.58 h-1); the conditional lowest-power passes (275 rpm at 0.35 vvm for 20 L at 354.77 W/m3 and kLa 40.80 h-1; 150 rpm at 0.35 vvm for 200 L at 317.46 W/m3 and kLa 39.95 h-1) are not robust to the declared sensitivity; and the preferred-strategy ranking reorders completely between gas-exponent assumptions of 0 and 0.8 (20 L lowest-power pass at 350 rpm and 0.15 vvm vs 225 rpm and 0.35 vvm). Copying the source recipe costs 763.19 W/m3 at 20 L (kLa 40.23 h-1) and 4208.27 W/m3 at 200 L (kLa 55.49 h-1), the latter about 4.2x the assumed power screen with tip speed 3.72 m/s. The scenario file's gauge pressure (100 kPa vs published 0.1-0.3 bar overhead), its kLa entry (20 h-1 vs the 38.8 h-1 target) and its OUR/solubility/cost entries are either unreconciled with or unused by the sulfolobus model, although its own numbers are internally self-consistent for oxygen transfer (20 x (7.5 x 0.7 - 1.5) = 75 mg/L/h vs assumed OUR 50 mg/L/h). Nothing in scope certifies a receiver operating point; withheld receiving outcomes and evaluator-only article access remain explicit gaps, and the 200 L data-quality caveats block process-level validation there.

workflow.assessment: The scoped package frames an aerobic-fermentation scale-transfer problem: match a source bioreactor's measured oxygen-transfer coefficient at larger receivers using two water-calibration summaries, published impeller geometry, and declared scenario assumptions. The transfer problem is reconstructed; it is not certified. The two calibration rows share a single airflow, so the gas-flow exponent is unidentified and every modeled receiver kLa is assumption-driven; the fitted power law has zero residual degrees of freedom and rests on rounded published summaries. The declared operating point fails the nominal kLa matching criterion under every gas-exponent value swept, and the conditional lowest-power screen passes are not robust to the declared sensitivity. Copying the source recipe is power-inefficient at the largest receiver. Rated equipment limits, tank diameter, sparger geometry, receiver broth characterization, oxygen uptake and medium solubility are absent, so no operating strategy can be certified and no oxygen-feasibility or biological-outcome claim is available. Every numerical result is a published summary, an author-calculated value, a fitted parameter, or a scenario assumption; none is a receiver measurement. The reference target's basis label conflicts with the scoped ring-sparger rows and stays unresolved. Engineering follow-up: characterize receiver broth kLa and the gas-flow exponent, obtain certified equipment limits, and reconcile the reference basis before any recipe decision. No equipment approval or control action is proposed here. Status: submitted as a partial investigation. The classified claim ledger covers the interpretation and hypothesis statements; the numeric observed-fact statements cannot be linked to numeric evidence rows because the scoped ingestion contains text-only lines with no numeric cells, so independent human review of those numeric statements against the original sources remains required.

interpretations.statement: The scoped package separates three evidence classes - direct water measurements (the two kLa rows), author-calculated or fitted quantities (power densities, tip speeds, geometry ratio), and declared scenario assumptions - and the transfer analysis inherits the weakest class: with both calibration rows at one airflow, gas-flow dependence is unidentified and any single recommended operating point is assumption-driven rather than measured.

Under the versioned transfer model the declared operating point does not meet the nominal kLa matching criterion for any gas-exponent value in the swept range, so its screen failure is robust to the unidentified exponent even though every other strategy ranking is not.

Copying the source recipe (same rpm and same specific airflow) is not power-neutral: receiver geometry with more submerged impellers and larger impeller diameters changes power density sharply, and at the largest receiver the modeled power density exceeds the assumed power screen by roughly a factor of four - a modeled result conditional on the constant turbulent power-number and gassing-factor hypotheses, not a measurement.

No absolute oxygen-feasibility claim is available: OUR, process-medium oxygen solubility and absolute DO for the Sulfolobus process are absent from the scoped evidence, and the scenario file's oxygen-uptake, solubility, saturation and price entries are declared assumptions that the versioned sulfolobus transfer model does not consume.

The reference target's basis label conflicts with the scoped calibration rows: the target value is labeled micro-sparger-based, but the only rows carrying that value in the fully-read package are ring-sparger rows, and no micro-sparger row exists in scope; either the label is inaccurate or the underlying row was withheld with the evaluator-only article, and the conflict cannot be resolved within scope.

The scenario's declared gauge pressure sits well above the published receiver overhead pressure range and is not reconciled with it, although the sulfolobus transfer model does not consume the pressure assumption. The overhead (gauge) reading of the published range is the consistent interpretation: an absolute reading would place the published range below one atmosphere and contradict the slight-overhead wording. This is a reconciliation gap between the scenario file and the cultivation evidence, not an equipment claim.

Process-level validation of any transfer strategy at the largest receiver is blocked by the reported data quality: viability was not measured and off-gas data were faulty there, and the calibration medium was water rather than fermentation broth, so modeled kLa matches cannot be read as biological success.

decision_branches.condition: Receiver broth kLa characterization at the preferred operating point lands materially below the water-based model prediction
actions_available_now: Schedule broth kLa characterization at the candidate setpoints

decision_branches.condition: Broth characterization is complete and shows materially lower transfer than the water-based model
actions_available_now: Re-screen operating points using the characterized broth surface; expect higher rpm or airflow demand

decision_branches.condition: Broth characterization confirms the water-based prediction within engineering tolerance
actions_available_now: Retain the conditional passes for engineering review with in-process DO monitoring

decision_branches.condition: Certified motor, torque, speed or vessel limits exclude the higher-power grid candidates
actions_available_now: Request vendor limit documentation for both receivers

decision_branches.condition: Certified limits restrict the candidate set
actions_available_now: Restrict the candidate set to points within certified limits and re-run the conditional screen

decision_branches.condition: Certified limits admit the lowest-power conditional passes
actions_available_now: Proceed with engineering review of the lowest-power conditional passes

decision_branches.condition: Full-article review shows the reference target basis is a distinct micro-sparger row rather than the scoped ring-sparger row
actions_available_now: Flag the basis-label conflict to the data curation owner

decision_branches.condition: A distinct micro-sparger row is found in the withheld article
actions_available_now: Re-derive the nominal kLa target and re-run the screen against the corrected basis

decision_branches.condition: The basis label is confirmed as a curation error
actions_available_now: Correct the curated basis label and confirm the ring-sparger target with the source authors

triage.reason: No policy rule matched verified categorical source signals.

evidence_requests.target: 20 L Infors Techfors S receiver broth kLa response surface in process medium
evidence_requests.reason: The fitted water-based model cannot certify receiver kLa; broth characterization at candidate setpoints is the action-changing evidence.

evidence_requests.target: source-scale kLa determination at a second airflow
evidence_requests.reason: The gas-flow exponent is unidentifiable from the two same-airflow rows and it reorders every conditional strategy ranking.

evidence_requests.target: certified equipment limits (motor power, safe rpm, safe torque, vessel pressure rating) for Infors HT Techfors S and Heinrich Frings Proreact 20P
evidence_requests.reason: No candidate can be screened for mechanical feasibility without certified limits; all rated-limit fields are missing in scope.

evidence_requests.target: full-article Table 2 micro-sparger rows and reference basis clarification (evaluator-controlled)
evidence_requests.reason: The reference target basis label conflicts with the scoped ring-sparger rows; the target drives every pass/fail decision.

evidence_requests.target: OUR and process-medium oxygen solubility at 75 degrees C and pH 3
evidence_requests.reason: No absolute oxygen-feasibility claim is possible without uptake and solubility data.

evidence_requests.target: receiver sparger geometry and tank diameter documentation
evidence_requests.reason: Sparger orifice geometry and tank diameter are missing for all vessels; geometry corrections are declared missing inputs.

follow_up_actions.action: Review the conditional screen passes and the fitted-model limitations before any recipe or setpoint decision; no implementation from this report
follow_up_actions.reason: All passing strategies are conditional on unvalidated water-based scaling and the model labels them engineering_review_required with rated feasibility unknown.

follow_up_actions.action: Independent review of this investigation, its measurement/fitted/assumption classification and the unresolved reference-basis conflict
follow_up_actions.reason: Human review is required; the automated layer certified no arithmetic because the scoped data has no numeric cells.

follow_up_actions.action: Plan receiver broth kLa characterization and gas-exponent identification experiments at the candidate setpoints

analysis.cross_scope_synthesis: Shared patterns: the two literature-oriented sources transcribe the same published package and agree on all overlapping values, so the calibration basis is internally consistent; the scenario source is of a different kind and declares an assumed receiver whose values are assumptions by construction. Exceptions: the receiver's declared air flow is inconsistent with its own vvm declaration and matches the largest published aeration envelope instead; the assumed kLa and OUR pair does not reproduce the published observation that pure oxygen was required at the normal pressure, so the receiver characterization is not calibrated to the source process; the scenario declares no temperature, pH, methanol feed or biomass target, so the published recipe is not transferred; and the source itself carries unresolved internal conflicts in the enzyme-production narrative values and in the standard-deviation wording. Limits: the package contains no numeric time series, no raw replicates, no geometry, no certified ratings and no kinetic model; the full article and the withheld receiving answers are evaluator-only. All quantitative strategy results are conditional on declared assumptions, and the deterministic layer cannot certify arithmetic from this package. A specialist cross-check child was spawned for an independent reconciliation review but did not return its subreport before the investigation phase closed; its work is explicitly unresolved and none of its findings are incorporated or cited.
analysis.assessment: The scoped evidence reconstructs a process-transfer problem: an optimized ten-litre Pichia high-cell-density fermentation from one published report (DOI 10.1038/srep18439, calibration-only excerpts; full article evaluator-only) is to be transferred to a receiving vessel that is described only by declared assumptions. The source supplies endpoint calibration, equipment operating envelopes and two reported pressure settings, but no trajectories, no measured kLa or OUR, no geometry and no certified pressure rating. Run on the declared assumptions, the host fermentation_transfer tool computes both conditional strategies as oxygen-transfer-feasible and ranks pressurized air at the increased pressure cheaper on partial oxygen-delivery cost than supplemental oxygen at the normal pressure; exact tool outputs are recorded in the resolved questions and are assumption-conditional, not measurements. The declared characterization is not calibrated to the published process: under the assumed kLa and OUR, air alone at the normal pressure would already cover the assumed uptake, yet the paper reports that supplemental pure oxygen was required at that pressure. Receiver kLa and OUR are therefore unvalidated, the flow declarations are internally inconsistent, and the certified vessel pressure rating, DO calibration convention and flow reference basis remain unverified. No equipment approval or control action is proposed; engineering characterization and human review are required before any transfer decision.

draft_report.assessment: The scoped evidence reconstructs a process-transfer problem: an optimized ten-litre Pichia high-cell-density fermentation from one published report (DOI 10.1038/srep18439, calibration-only excerpts; full article evaluator-only) is to be transferred to a receiving vessel that is described only by declared assumptions. The source supplies endpoint calibration, equipment operating envelopes and two reported pressure settings, but no trajectories, no measured kLa or OUR, no geometry and no certified pressure rating. Run on the declared assumptions, the host fermentation_transfer tool computes both conditional strategies as oxygen-transfer-feasible and ranks pressurized air at the increased pressure cheaper on partial oxygen-delivery cost than supplemental oxygen at the normal pressure; exact tool outputs are recorded in the resolved questions and are assumption-conditional, not measurements. The declared characterization is not calibrated to the published process: under the assumed kLa and OUR, air alone at the normal pressure would already cover the assumed uptake, yet the paper reports that supplemental pure oxygen was required at that pressure. Receiver kLa and OUR are therefore unvalidated, the flow declarations are internally inconsistent, and the certified vessel pressure rating, DO calibration convention and flow reference basis remain unverified. No equipment approval or control action is proposed; engineering characterization and human review are required before any transfer decision.

The scoped literature package is a calibration-only excerpt set for one published research report on Pichia pastoris high-cell-density fermentation (DOI 10.1038/srep18439, PMC4726300); the full article is evaluator-only, and withheld receiving answers must not be inferred.

The published ten-litre optimized endpoint calibration reports volumetric enzyme activity with a reported standard deviation over three parallel measurements or independent assays; independent fermentations were not established, and the table footnote's standard-deviation wording conflicts with the methods' standard-error wording.
The published volumetric enzyme production endpoint is derived from enzyme activity and differs slightly from the Results narrative value due to rounding; the source retains the table value.
The published biomass at the reported peak sampling time and the sampling time itself are transcribed in the cited facts; the sampling time is a reported observation time, not a process clock.

Published derived biomass-normalized outcomes (biomass enzyme production, specific enzyme production rate, and an approximately zero specific growth rate) carry reported standard deviations over three parallel measurements or independent assays.

Published optimized conditions include a temperature band, a pH setpoint, a nominal gauge pressure with a reported operating band, a methanol feed rate per unit biomass, an induction dissolved-oxygen setpoint of one percent, an initial induction biomass, and no supplemental pure oxygen.

Two reported pressure settings exist in the source, a normal setting and an increased nominal setting, with a source-text operating band that the source explicitly interprets as a reported operating range rather than a standard deviation or probability distribution; absolute pressure requires adding separately assumed or measured ambient pressure.

The published equipment set spans four nominal vessel sizes with reported aeration and agitation operating envelopes; flow reference conditions are not reported, and pressure ratings, motor power, impeller diameter and sparger geometry are null in the scoped transcription.

The source's missing-input list includes measured kLa, OUR, medium oxygen solubility, DO calibration convention, inlet pure oxygen flow, exhaust oxygen, flow reference conditions, broth hydrodynamics, gas pressure drop, shaft power, methanol feed integral and cost, cooling and occupancy costs, certified vessel pressure rating, DO calibration reference at operating pressure, and replicated feed, gas and productivity trajectories.

Source limitations state that the direct oxygen comparison was performed in a thirty-litre vessel; that scale-up outcomes also change feeding, dissolved oxygen and biomass; that no Pichia kinetic model is calibrated and pressure does not predict enzyme productivity; and that reported costs are hypothetical oxygen-delivery costs.

The source flags an internal numerical conflict among the enzyme-production narrative values and retains the table value with a conflict flag; standard-deviation versus standard-error wording is also inconsistent in the published methods.

The declared receiver scenario assumptions specify a selected receiver volume, an agitation rate, an airflow in vvm, a gauge pressure, an ambient pressure, air and supplemental-oxygen flows, a compressor efficiency and inlet temperature, electricity and oxygen prices, a comparison window, an air-saturation value, a broth solubility factor, a kLa, a dissolved-oxygen value, an OUR, a methanol price, a gas exponent and a power screen; every one of these values is an assumption, not a measurement.

draft_report.cross_scope_synthesis: Shared patterns: the two literature-oriented sources transcribe the same published package and agree on all overlapping values, so the calibration basis is internally consistent; the scenario source is of a different kind and declares an assumed receiver whose values are assumptions by construction. Exceptions: the receiver's declared air flow is inconsistent with its own vvm declaration and matches the largest published aeration envelope instead; the assumed kLa and OUR pair does not reproduce the published observation that pure oxygen was required at the normal pressure, so the receiver characterization is not calibrated to the source process; the scenario declares no temperature, pH, methanol feed or biomass target, so the published recipe is not transferred; and the source itself carries unresolved internal conflicts in the enzyme-production narrative values and in the standard-deviation wording. Limits: the package contains no numeric time series, no raw replicates, no geometry, no certified ratings and no kinetic model; the full article and the withheld receiving answers are evaluator-only. All quantitative strategy results are conditional on declared assumptions, and the deterministic layer cannot certify arithmetic from this package. A specialist cross-check child was spawned for an independent reconciliation review but did not return its subreport before the investigation phase closed; its work is explicitly unresolved and none of its findings are incorporated or cited.

resolved_questions.question: What are the published pressure settings and how is the reported band interpreted?
resolved_questions.finding: Normal 0.05 MPa gauge and increased nominal 0.1 MPa gauge, verified against source bytes (verify_evidence: source_integrity true, value_matches true). The source text form '0.10 ± 0.05 MPa super-atmospheric pressure' is a reported operating band, not an SD or probability distribution; absolute pressure adds separately assumed/measured ambient pressure.

resolved_questions.question: What are the declared receiver parameters and their epistemic status?
resolved_questions.finding: Selected receiver 20 L, 300 rpm, 0.25 vvm, 100 kPa gauge, ambient 101.325 kPa, air 36 Nm3/h, supplemental O2 2 Nm3/h, compressor efficiency 0.65, inlet 303.15 K, electricity 0.12 USD/kWh, oxygen 0.20 USD/Nm3, comparison window 120 h, air saturation 7.5 mg/L, broth solubility factor 0.7, kLa 20 1/h, DO 1.5 mg/L, OUR 50 mg/L/h, methanol 0.5 USD/L, gas exponent 0.5, power screen 1000 W/m3. Every value is a scenario assumption, not a measurement.

resolved_questions.question: HOST-TOOL RESULT (base run, declared assumptions; registered deterministic characterization, assumption-conditional, not a measurement): what do the two conditional strategies compute to?
resolved_questions.finding: Supplemental oxygen at 50 kPa gauge (air 36 + O2 2 Nm3/h): P_abs 151.325 kPa, inlet O2 fraction about 0.2511, C* about 9.398 mg/L, OTR about 157.96 mg/L/h, OUR margin about +107.96 mg/L/h, compressor about 0.694 kW, partial cost about 0.4833 USD/h. Pressurized air at 100 kPa gauge (air 36 Nm3/h, no O2): P_abs 201.325 kPa, inlet O2 fraction 0.2095, C* about 10.431 mg/L, OTR about 178.63 mg/L/h, margin about +128.63 mg/L/h, compressor about 1.188 kW, partial cost about 0.1425 USD/h. Air-only saturation ratio (100 vs 50 kPa gauge) about 1.3304. conditional_oxygen_feasible true; equipment_pressure_rating_verified false; biology_prediction null; empirical baseline 32,000,000 U/L and 640 mg/L flagged as constant ten-litre endpoint, not pressure kinetics.

resolved_questions.question: HOST-TOOL RESULT (economics, declared assumptions): which strategy is cheaper and by how much?
resolved_questions.finding: Savings about 0.3407 USD/h, about 40.89 USD over the 120 h comparison window; break-even purchased-oxygen price about 0.0296 USD/Nm3 against an assumed 0.20 USD/Nm3. Excluded: cooling, agitation electricity, occupancy, capital, downstream recovery, methanol unless specified. Flow basis: Nm3 at 273.15 K and 101.325 kPa; paper flow reference conditions unknown.

resolved_questions.question: HOST-TOOL RESULT (sensitivity variants, declared assumptions): how robust is the comparison?
resolved_questions.finding: (a) Air-only at the published normal pressure 50 kPa (no O2): OTR about 126.81 mg/L/h, margin about +76.81 mg/L/h, cost about 0.0833 USD/h - so the declared kLa/OUR assumptions do not reproduce the published need for supplemental oxygen at that pressure. workflow.cross_scope_synthesis: Shared patterns: the two literature-oriented sources transcribe the same published package and agree on all overlapping values, so the calibration basis is internally consistent; the scenario source is of a different kind and declares an assumed receiver whose values are assumptions by construction. Exceptions: the receiver's declared air flow is inconsistent with its own vvm declaration and matches the largest published aeration envelope instead; the assumed kLa and OUR pair does not reproduce the published observation that pure oxygen was required at the normal pressure, so the receiver characterization is not calibrated to the source process; the scenario declares no temperature, pH, methanol feed or biomass target, so the published recipe is not transferred; and the source itself carries unresolved internal conflicts in the enzyme-production narrative values and in the standard-deviation wording. Limits: the package contains no numeric time series, no raw replicates, no geometry, no certified ratings and no kinetic model; the full article and the withheld receiving answers are evaluator-only. All quantitative strategy results are conditional on declared assumptions, and the deterministic layer cannot certify arithmetic from this package. A specialist cross-check child was spawned for an independent reconciliation review but did not return its subreport before the investigation phase closed; its work is explicitly unresolved and none of its findings are incorporated or cited.
workflow.objective: Reconstruct the transfer problem from the scoped literature excerpts. Reconcile source and receiver parameters; identify missing characterization. Use the host fermentation_transfer(assumptions={...}) tool through the existing bridge for numerical calculations. Compare conditional operating strategies, cite the retrieved source evidence and distinguish measurements, fitted values and assumptions. Report limitations and engineering follow-up; never approve or control equipment. Do not retrieve external literature or infer the withheld receiving answers.
workflow.assessment: The scoped evidence reconstructs a process-transfer problem: an optimized ten-litre Pichia high-cell-density fermentation from one published report (DOI 10.1038/srep18439, calibration-only excerpts; full article evaluator-only) is to be transferred to a receiving vessel that is described only by declared assumptions. The source supplies endpoint calibration, equipment operating envelopes and two reported pressure settings, but no trajectories, no measured kLa or OUR, no geometry and no certified pressure rating. Run on the declared assumptions, the host fermentation_transfer tool computes both conditional strategies as oxygen-transfer-feasible and ranks pressurized air at the increased pressure cheaper on partial oxygen-delivery cost than supplemental oxygen at the normal pressure; exact tool outputs are recorded in the resolved questions and are assumption-conditional, not measurements. The declared characterization is not calibrated to the published process: under the assumed kLa and OUR, air alone at the normal pressure would already cover the assumed uptake, yet the paper reports that supplemental pure oxygen was required at that pressure. Receiver kLa and OUR are therefore unvalidated, the flow declarations are internally inconsistent, and the certified vessel pressure rating, DO calibration convention and flow reference basis remain unverified. No equipment approval or control action is proposed; engineering characterization and human review are required before any transfer decision.
